data.name: Business Signs
intro: Business signage does more work than almost anything else you'll buy for your premises. It tells people you're there, shows them the way in, and sets the tone before anyone has spoken to you. We design and make business signs for shops, offices, pubs, cafés, schools, sites and car parks, from a single door sign to a full set for a new building.

Start with the type of sign you need. [Acrylic signs](/business-signs/acrylic-signs/) and [3D letters](/business-signs/3d-letters/) give receptions and offices a polished finish. [Dibond aluminium signs](/business-signs/dibond-aluminium-signs/) and [outdoor signs](/business-signs/outdoor-signs/) are built to stand up to Norfolk weather. [Illuminated signs](/business-signs/illuminated-signs/) keep you visible after dark, and [pavement signs](/business-signs/pavement-signs/) pull passing trade through the door.

Every sign is made to order. Choose the size, material and fixings on the product page, send us your logo or wording, and we'll send a proof to approve before anything goes into production. If you don't have artwork, our design studio can set it up for you or create something new.

Not sure what will work? Tell us where the sign is going, how far away people will read it from and whether it's inside or out, and we'll recommend the right product. We can also fit signs for businesses across Norfolk and Suffolk.

data.name: 3D Letters
intro: 3D letters turn your name or logo into something people notice. Built-up lettering stands proud of the wall and catches the light, so even a simple name looks considered and premium. They're popular for receptions, shopfronts, showrooms and office walls.

Choose from acrylic, metal and foamex letters. Acrylic letters come in gloss or matt black and white, or painted to any RAL colour to match your brand. Metal letters are available in brushed aluminium, stainless steel and gold finishes. Foamex and polystyrene letters are light and economical for large-scale or temporary displays.

Letters are cut from your artwork, so your font and logo stay exactly as designed. Fix them flat with strong tape, or on hidden stand-offs for a floating shadow effect. We supply a paper template so each letter goes in the right place.

For a sign that works after dark, see our [illuminated letters](/business-signs/illuminated-signs/). Comparing styles? Read [built-up letters vs flat panel signs](/signage-home/compare/built-up-letters-vs-flat-panel-signs/), or see our [built-up 3D letters service](/signage-home/building-signage-shop-signs/built-up-3d-letters/) for fitted shopfront lettering.

description: 3D metal letters give your business name a premium, permanent presence on reception walls, shopfronts and building entrances. Metal has a weight and quality that other materials can't quite match: it catches the light, casts crisp shadows and tells visitors you've invested in your brand.

Letters are cut from your own font or logo, so your branding stays exactly as designed. Choose a thickness of 3mm, 5mm or 10mm and a finish to suit your space, from brushed metal for a contemporary, understated look to polished or painted finishes for a bolder statement. Thicker letters stand further from the wall and cast stronger shadows, especially when mounted on hidden stand-offs.

Metal letters are suitable indoors and out. On a reception wall they create an instant focal point; outside, on a fascia, brick wall or entrance canopy, they give a building a smart, architectural identity that lasts for years with very little care.

Because every project is different, tell us your wording or logo, the size of the wall and where the letters are going, and we'll recommend the right metal, thickness and fixing, then send a proof before anything is made.

See also [gold metal letters](/business-signs/3d-letters/gold-metal-letters/) and [brushed aluminium letters](/business-signs/3d-letters/brushed-aluminium-letters/), or compare [built-up letters vs flat panel signs](/signage-home/compare/built-up-letters-vs-flat-panel-signs/).

data.name: Acrylic Signs
intro: Acrylic signs are the go-to choice for offices, receptions, salons and clinics that want a clean, modern look. The material is rigid, glossy and crisp at the edges, and it takes print beautifully, so your logo looks sharp and colours stay bright.

Most of our acrylic signs are printed on the back of a clear or coloured panel. Viewed from the front, the print sits behind a protective layer of acrylic, which gives it depth and keeps it safe from scratches and cleaning. A white ink layer behind the colours stops them looking washed out on clear material.

Choose from clear, frosted, black, white, glass-effect, recycled and glitter acrylic. Panels come as rectangles or can be cut to the outline of your logo, and you can pick from 3mm, 5mm and 10mm thicknesses on many signs. Thicker acrylic looks more substantial on a wall, especially when mounted on stand-offs.

Fixing options include polished stand-offs, which hold the sign away from the wall for a floating effect, as well as hidden fixings and adhesive pads for walls you'd rather not drill. Acrylic is suitable for indoor use and many signs work outside too; check each product for details.

Acrylic is often called Perspex, a well-known brand of the same material. Comparing options? See our [built-up letters vs flat panel signs guide](/signage-home/compare/built-up-letters-vs-flat-panel-signs/) or browse [3D letters](/business-signs/3d-letters/).

data.name: Correx Signs
intro: Correx signs are the quick, low-cost answer for temporary signage. Correx is fluted polypropylene board, the twin-wall plastic you see on estate agent boards, building sites and event signs. It's waterproof, very light and tough enough to survive being moved around.
We print correx in full colour, in sizes up to 2440mm x 1220mm. Boards can be cable-tied to railings and Heras fencing, fixed to posts or stakes, or simply screwed to a fence.

Use correx for site signs, directional signs for events, open days and car boot sales, political and campaign signs, and short-term promotions. For signs that need to last years, choose [Dibond aluminium](/business-signs/dibond-aluminium-signs/) instead.

See how correx compares in our [foamex vs aluminium composite vs correx guide](/signage-home/compare/foamex-vs-aluminium-composite-vs-correx/), or browse [construction site signs](/business-signs/hoarding-boards/).

data.name: Aluminium Signs
intro: Dibond signs are the workhorse of outdoor business signage. Dibond is a brand of aluminium composite panel: two thin skins of aluminium bonded to a solid core. It's rigid, flat, light enough to fix easily, and it won't rot, rust or warp in the weather.

We print directly onto the panel in full colour, so you can have photos, gradients and brand colours rather than just simple lettering. For exposed sites we add a protective laminate, including an anti-graffiti finish that lets paint and marker pen be cleaned off without damaging the print.

Choose from white, black, brushed silver and brushed brass-effect panels. Signs can be rectangular, cut to the outline of your logo, or folded into a tray sign with returned edges for shop fascias and building fronts.

Aluminium signs suit building exteriors, car parks, gates, schools, industrial units and anywhere a sign needs to last for years outdoors. Indoors, brushed finishes look smart in offices and receptions. Fix them flat with screw caps, float them on stand-offs, or mount them on [posts](/business-signs/outdoor-signs/).

Weighing up materials? Our [foamex vs aluminium composite vs correx comparison](/signage-home/compare/foamex-vs-aluminium-composite-vs-correx/) explains the differences, and we also make [aluminium composite panels](/signage-home/large-format-print/aluminium-composite-panels/) for larger projects.

description: Textured surface floor graphics grip brick, block paving and rough walls where normal vinyl won't stick. The specialist material is heated into the surface so the print follows every contour, with an R12 anti-slip rating.
Every floor graphic is made to measure. Tell us where it's going and how long it needs to last, and we'll recommend the right material and send a proof.
Floor graphics catch attention where people are already looking, which makes them one of the most effective ways to guide visitors and promote products.

Multi-surface vinyl solves a problem every event organiser and retailer has met: normal vinyl simply won't stick to brick, block paving, rough concrete or textured render. This specialist film conforms to the surface when heated, so your graphic follows every contour and grips firmly.

Use it for festival and event wayfinding, pavement promotions outside shops, branded walkways, sports venue graphics and temporary murals on textured walls. The R12 anti-slip finish provides strong grip underfoot.

This film is also used inside, for example on textured warehouse floors, on exposed brick in bars and on concrete in showrooms, where normal floor graphics won't hold. It's a temporary to medium-term solution, ideal for campaigns, events and seasonal routes.
Lifespan depends on footfall, weather and the surface. On a busy pavement in winter it may need replacing sooner than on a sheltered wall. We'll advise on expected lifespan for your location.

Because it bonds into textured surfaces, removal can take longer than with normal floor graphics. On most surfaces it can be peeled away with gentle heat; on very porous surfaces some cleaning may be needed afterwards. We'll advise on removal when you order.
Good design matters on the ground: use large, simple shapes, bold arrows and short words so people can read the graphic while walking.

data.name: Foamex Signs
intro: Foamex signs are light, rigid and great value. Foamex is a brand name for foam PVC board: a smooth, solid plastic sheet with a lightweight core. It prints well, cuts cleanly and is easy to fix, which makes it a favourite for shop signs, menus, exhibitions, office signs and short-term outdoor use.
We print foamex boards in full colour, most commonly on 5mm white board. Black and recycled boards are also available, and any board can be cut to the outline of your logo or a custom shape.

Indoors, foamex lasts for years. Outdoors it's best for short to medium-term signs, such as promotions, events and temporary site signs, because strong sun and temperature changes can make it bow over time. For permanent outdoor signs we'd usually suggest [Dibond aluminium](/business-signs/dibond-aluminium-signs/).
Compare materials in our [foamex vs aluminium composite vs correx guide](/signage-home/compare/foamex-vs-aluminium-composite-vs-correx/).

data.name: Hanging Signs
intro: Hanging signs are the traditional way to catch the eye of people walking along the street. Mounted on a bracket at right angles to the building, they're visible from both directions, which a flat fascia sign can't manage. Pubs, cafés, boutiques, galleries and high-street shops all use them.

We make hanging and projecting signs in metal, slate, foam PVC and printed panels, in square, round, rectangular and logo shapes. Most are printed on both sides. Brackets are available, or we can make signs to fit an existing bracket if you send us its measurements.

If your premises is in a conservation area or is a listed building, there may be rules on the size, material and style of hanging signs. Natural finishes such as slate and painted metal are often well received. Our [planning consent for shop signs guide](/signage-home/guides-and-advice/planning-consent-for-shop-signs/) has more detail.

Want it lit? See our [illuminated hanging sign](/business-signs/hanging-signs/illuminated-hanging-sign/) and [projecting light boxes](/business-signs/lightbox-signs/), or our fitted [projecting signs service](/signage-home/building-signage-shop-signs/projecting-signs/).

description: A hanging bar sign hangs from a bar bracket, so it's easy to see from along the pavement. The printed foam PVC panel is light, affordable and quick to put up.
Print it on one or both sides. It's ideal for shops, salons, cafés and offices on busy streets, and for temporary or seasonal signs.

The hanging bar format is one of the most practical ways to add a projecting sign to a shopfront. The sign panel hangs from a horizontal bar on a wall bracket, so it sits out over the pavement where people walking along the street can see it from both directions, long before they reach your window.

The 600mm foam PVC panel is lightweight, so the bracket and fixings don't need to be heavy-duty, and it's quick to put up or replace. Print it on one side or both, with your logo, opening hours, a QR code or a seasonal message. Because the panel is affordable, many businesses keep a spare or change it with the seasons.

It's popular with independent shops, salons, cafés, barbers, studios and offices above shops, where a full fascia sign isn't possible. For a more permanent, premium sign, consider our [metal hanging sign](/business-signs/hanging-signs/metal-hanging-sign/) or [slate hanging sign](/business-signs/hanging-signs/slate-hanging-sign/).

Projecting signs are often covered by planning rules, especially in conservation areas and on listed buildings. A small hanging sign at ground floor level is frequently allowed under deemed consent, but rules vary by area, height and illumination. We can advise on typical requirements, and if you need to apply for consent we'll provide the drawings and dimensions you need.

When positioning the sign, the bottom of the panel should normally be at least 2.6m above the pavement so that people can walk underneath safely, and the bracket must be fixed into sound masonry. Our fitting team installs hanging signs across Norfolk and Suffolk, or we can supply everything with fixings for your own installer.

Design tip: keep the message short. People walking past have a few seconds to read a projecting sign, so a bold logo and one or two words, such as the type of business, works better than a long list of services.

Hanging bar signs work particularly well on narrow streets and in arcades, where people walk close to shopfronts and a fascia sign is hard to see. They also suit businesses on upper floors or down side passages, where a projecting sign at street level points customers in the right direction.

For a cohesive look, match the panel design to your fascia, window graphics and A-board. Using the same colours, fonts and logo across all your signs makes your business easier to recognise from the street.

Post-mounted signs put your panel on one or two posts at the height you need, with post lengths, colours and bases to suit the ground. Panels are made from durable, weatherproof materials such as aluminium composite. Larger freestanding signs need secure foundations, and may need planning consent, so speak to us about installation.

description: Bollard covers turn the plain bollards around your car park, forecourt or venue into eye-catching advertising and wayfinding. Printed correx sleeves slip over existing bollards, so there's nothing to install.
They're sold in packs of 10, in a range of diameters and heights to fit common bollards. Use them for branding, promotions, event sponsorship, car park directions or safety messages.
Because they're printed on light, weatherproof correx, they're affordable enough to change with each campaign.

Bollard covers are a clever way to use space you already have. Car parks, forecourts and venues often have rows of plain bollards in prime positions; wrapping them in printed sleeves turns each one into a small billboard at eye level.
They're ideal for seasonal promotions, sponsor branding at events, and directing visitors around a site.
Covers are printed on durable, weather-resistant material and are quick to fit and remove, so they can be changed for each event or season without tools.
Tell us the height and diameter of your bollards and we'll size the covers to suit.
Bollard covers are used at sports grounds, retail parks, garden centres and festivals. They're also great for sponsors at events.

description: A curved totem sign is one of the most effective ways to announce your business at a site entrance. Standing up to three metres tall, it's seen from the road, from the car park and from across a business estate, long before anyone reaches your door. The gently curved faces catch the light and give the sign a modern, architectural shape that a flat board can't match.

Each totem is built around a welded aluminium tray, powder coated in the RAL colour of your choice, with a steel framework inside for strength. Your graphics are digitally printed, laminated for protection and applied to the front, or to both front and back so the sign works for traffic coming from either direction. The result is a solid, freestanding monolith that looks at home outside offices, retail parks, schools, hotels, care homes and industrial units.

Choose from four standard sizes: 1000 or 1500mm wide, and 2000 or 3000mm tall. If those don't suit your site, we can make the totem to a bespoke size, add 3D lettering or logos to the faces, or build in illumination so it stays visible after dark.

A totem is a long-term investment in your site's first impression, so it's worth planning it properly. Think about where drivers will first see it, how far away they'll be when they need to read it, and what they need to know: your name, a logo, perhaps the businesses on a shared site and a phone number or web address. Keep it simple and it will work hard for years.

Comparing styles? The [flat totem sign](/business-signs/outdoor-signs/totem-sign/) has the same construction with flat faces. Browse all [outdoor signs](/business-signs/outdoor-signs/) or read [how long outdoor signs last](/signage-home/guides-and-advice/how-long-do-outdoor-signs-last/).

description: Totem signs give your business a confident, permanent presence at the edge of your site. This flat totem stands as a freestanding monolith up to three metres tall, so drivers and visitors can spot your entrance from a distance and know they've arrived.

It's built from a welded aluminium tray powder coated in your choice of RAL colour, supported by an internal steel frame. Printed, laminated graphics are applied to one or both faces, giving you room for your name, logo, the businesses on a shared site, directions or contact details.

Choose from four standard sizes, 1000 or 1500mm wide and 2000 or 3000mm tall, or ask for a bespoke size. Flat faces give a crisp, classic look that suits corporate sites, schools, medical centres, retail parks and industrial estates. Add 3D letters or illumination if you want the sign to stand out even more.

When planning your totem, think about reading distance: a sign seen from a road needs large, simple lettering and strong contrast. We'll help you lay out the design and show you a proof before production.

data.name: Parking Signs
intro: Parking signs keep car parks organised and make it clear who can park where. Whether you're reserving bays for staff and visitors, marking disabled spaces or setting out rules for a private car park, clear signs prevent arguments and keep traffic moving safely.

Our car park signs cover visitor, staff, customer, permit, residents and disabled parking, as well as speed limits, reverse parking, directional arrows and private road and property notices. Most are available in several sizes, in portrait or landscape, and many come with arrow options.

Signs are made from weatherproof materials for outdoor use and can be fixed to walls, fences or posts. If you need different wording, your logo, or a whole set of matching signs for a site, we can make custom parking signs to order.

Looking for signs to stop people parking? See [no parking signs](/business-signs/parking-signs/no-parking-signs/). For more safety signage, browse our [safety and warning signs](/signage-home/site-safety-signs/safety-and-warning-signs/).

data.name: No Parking Signs
intro: No parking signs protect your access: driveways, gates, entrances, garages and loading bays. A clear, polite sign is often all it takes to stop people blocking you in.

Choose from standard no parking signs and specific messages such as 'Do not block driveway', 'No parking in front of these gates', 'Access required 24 hours' and 'Keep entrance clear'. Many come with a 'Polite notice' header option, which tends to get a better response from neighbours and visitors.
Signs are weatherproof, in sizes from A4 up to 80cm wide, and can be fixed to walls, gates, fences or posts. Need different wording? We can make custom no parking signs too.

A sign on private property shows your wishes, but it doesn't make obstructing a driveway a criminal offence on its own. For managed car parks and enforcement, see our [parking signs](/business-signs/parking-signs/).

data.name: Pavement Signs
intro: Pavement signs and A-boards are one of the cheapest ways to bring passing trade through your door. Put your offer, menu or opening hours right where people walk, and change the message whenever you like.

Choose the style that suits your business. Printed A-boards carry your branding in full colour. Chalkboard A-boards let you write daily specials. Poster and snap-frame A-boards let you swap printed posters in seconds. Swinging and spring-based pavement signs move with the wind instead of blowing over, which makes them ideal for exposed forecourts.

Wooden A-boards in natural, painted and whitewashed finishes suit cafés, pubs and independent shops, while steel and plastic frames are tough and practical. We also make tabletop chalkboards and framed wall chalkboards for inside.

Placing an A-board on the public pavement may need permission or a licence from your council, and it must leave room for pedestrians, wheelchairs and pushchairs. Check the rules where you trade. For seating areas, see our [cafe barriers](/business-signs/cafe-barriers/).

description: A branded A-board puts your logo on premium panels: brushed silver, mirror or satin black, set into a wooden frame for a high-end look outside salons, boutiques and hotels. Wood looks warm and welcoming on the street and suits independent and heritage businesses especially well.
Choose 550 x 800mm or 750 x 1100mm. Timber frames are sturdy and repairable, and panels can be reprinted when your branding or menu changes.

The panels are what make this A-board special. Brushed silver gives a contemporary, metallic look; mirror panels catch the light and reflect the street; satin black gives a sleek, understated finish. Your logo and message are printed onto the panel, set into a solid wooden frame.

It's a premium alternative to standard printed A-boards, chosen by salons, boutiques, hotels, jewellers and restaurants that want their pavement sign to match the quality of their interior. Panels can be reprinted when your branding changes, so the frame keeps working for years.

The wooden frame gives a warm, natural look that suits independent businesses, high streets, market towns and seaside locations, and pairs particularly well with timber shopfronts. With occasional treatment using a wood oil or preserver, the frame keeps its colour and resists weathering.
Because the panels slot into the frame, you can choose a different panel finish for each side, for example a branded panel facing one way and a different message facing the other.

This A-board makes a strong first impression outside premium businesses. A brushed or mirror panel with a crisp printed logo looks closer to a permanent shop sign than a temporary pavement board, which helps customers see quality before they walk in.

Before placing any A-board on the pavement, check your council's rules. Many require a licence or set limits on where boards can stand, so there's always a clear path for pedestrians, wheelchairs and pushchairs. Placing the board close to your shopfront usually keeps it within the rules.

description: A whiteboard A-board lets you write in dry-wipe marker for bold, colourful messages that wipe clean in seconds.
The wooden frame holds whiteboard panels on both sides.

Dry-wipe A-boards suit businesses that want colourful, eye-catching messages without chalk dust. Write in bright marker colours, add drawings and arrows, and wipe it clean at the end of the day. It's a great fit for cafés, salons, gift shops and garden centres.
The wooden frame folds flat for storage and is sturdy enough for daily use. Bring it in at night and in heavy rain to keep the timber and whiteboard panels in good condition.

A dry-wipe A-board is also useful inside: for welcome messages in hotel lobbies, room directions at events, today's classes in gyms, or queue information in shops. Many businesses use one outside and one inside.

For neat, readable lettering, write the key words large, use one or two colours, and leave space around the message. Bright colours such as red, blue and green show up well against the white surface from a distance, and a simple drawing or arrow helps catch the eye.

The board's white surface makes colour pop, so it suits businesses that change their message often: daily coffee specials, today's cakes, class timetables, walk-in availability at salons, or plant offers at garden centres. A dry-wipe A-board also works well for events, where directions and times change through the day.
Keep a cloth and a set of markers near the door so staff can update it quickly, and clean the whole surface regularly with whiteboard cleaner to stop ghost marks building up.

Every graphic is made to measure: send your wall dimensions and a photo and we'll advise on the right material and layout, then send a proof. Our design studio can create artwork from your brand guidelines or photography.
Wall graphics are one of the most cost-effective ways to transform a space, and most can be removed or updated later as your business changes.

Brick wall vinyl opens up exterior walls for advertising and decoration without painting. Gable ends, side walls, car park walls and courtyards can carry your branding, a mural or wayfinding, with the brick texture showing through the print for a painted-on look.

The film is designed for rough, textured surfaces and is heated into the brick and mortar during application, so it follows every contour and stays bonded outdoors. It's best applied by experienced fitters; we install across Norfolk and Suffolk.
It's a fraction of the cost of a hand-painted mural, and can be removed later, making it ideal for temporary campaigns and rented buildings.

Before fitting, we check the wall for loose mortar, flaking paint and damp, all of which can affect adhesion. Clean, dry, sound brick gives the best result. Application is best done in dry weather above 10°C.
It's popular with pubs, breweries, garden centres, schools and businesses with large blank side walls, as well as councils and community groups for public art.

Exterior wall graphics can need planning consent if they advertise a business, especially in conservation areas or on listed buildings. Decorative murals may be treated differently. Check with your local planning authority before installing a large graphic on an outside wall.
Our studio can design murals from your brand, local history or photography, and mock them up on a photo of your wall so you can see the result before it's printed.

description: Chalkboard wall vinyl turns any smooth wall into a chalkboard for menus, notes, planning and creativity. It's popular in cafés, kitchens, classrooms and creative offices.

Wall graphics are one of the most cost-effective ways to transform a space, and most can be removed or updated later as your business changes.

Chalkboard wall vinyl brings the charm of a blackboard to any smooth wall, without the mess and expense of chalkboard paint. It goes on as a single smooth sheet, made to measure for your space, and gives a deep matt black surface that's ready to write on straight away.

Use it for café and restaurant menus, specials boards, shop window-side displays, office idea walls, kitchen planners and classroom boards. Chalk pens give bright, bold lettering that wipes off with a damp cloth, while traditional chalk gives a softer, classic look.

Because it's vinyl, it can be removed later from sound, well-cured paint, which makes it ideal for rented premises and pop-ups. We can also print a permanent header, logo or border onto the chalkboard surface so your branding stays fixed while the menu changes.

In hospitality, a chalkboard wall becomes part of the experience. A large menu wall behind the counter, a beer and wine list beside the bar, or a hand-lettered quote in a dining area gives a relaxed, crafted feel that customers photograph and share. Because the vinyl covers the whole area in one even sheet, there's none of the patchy finish that chalkboard paint can give.

In offices and schools, chalkboard walls encourage people to write, sketch and share ideas. They're a softer alternative to whiteboards in creative spaces and breakout areas, and work well for weekly targets, team shout-outs and event notices. At home, they're popular in kitchens for shopping lists and family planners, and in children's rooms for drawing.

To keep the surface looking its best, wipe chalk pen off with a damp cloth and dry it afterwards. Prime with chalk before first use if you plan to use traditional chalk, by rubbing the side of a stick over the whole surface and wiping it off; this reduces ghosting from your first messages.

Chalkboard vinyl can also be cut to shape, such as a speech bubble, a circle, a coffee cup or a price label, for a playful feature on a wall or door. Shaped chalkboards are popular in cafés and shops for daily specials and in children's rooms for drawing. Tell us the shape you have in mind and we'll create it.

description: Clear wall vinyl prints your design onto a transparent film, so feature walls, brick, wood or glass show through. It's perfect when you want graphics without hiding an attractive surface.

Every graphic is made to measure: send your wall dimensions and a photo and we'll advise on the right material and layout, then send a proof. Our design studio can create artwork from your brand guidelines or photography.
Wall graphics are one of the most cost-effective ways to transform a space, and most can be removed or updated later as your business changes.

Clear wall vinyl is the solution when the wall itself is part of the design. On exposed brick, timber cladding, polished plaster or coloured paint, a clear film lets the surface show through around your print, so the graphic looks painted on rather than stuck on. It's ideal for logos, wording and illustrations in cafés, bars, studios and offices with character.

We print using white ink beneath the colours where needed, so your design stays bright and solid on darker backgrounds, while unprinted areas remain transparent. Clear vinyl also works on glass and gloss surfaces, making it a versatile choice for partitions and feature walls.

Because it's made to measure, you can cover a small area with a logo or a whole feature wall. Send us a photo of the surface and we'll advise whether clear vinyl or a cut-vinyl alternative will give the best result.

Clear vinyl is also a clever way to brand glass meeting rooms and partitions without blocking the view. A logo, strapline or decorative band printed on clear film keeps rooms bright while adding privacy cues and your branding, and it can be combined with frosted manifestation for safety markings at eye level.

On painted walls, clear vinyl can be the right choice where your wall colour is already part of the brand palette. Instead of printing a large background to match the paint, which can show a slight colour difference, the paint itself becomes the background and the print sits on top. It's a neater result on feature walls in brand colours.

We'll check your artwork before printing and advise where white ink is needed. Thin lines and small text print well, and we can show a mock-up of the design on a photo of your wall so you can see exactly how the wall colour will interact with the print before anything is produced.

Clear vinyl is printed with a protective laminate so the colours resist scuffs and fading. The finished film is thin, so it sits flat on the wall with almost no visible edge, which is what gives the painted-on effect. Fitting is best done by experienced installers, because bubbles and dust are more visible on clear film than on white vinyl.

description: Repositionable wall graphics are printed on a fabric that peels off and sticks again cleanly. They're perfect for rented offices, pop-ups and campaigns that change, because they leave walls undamaged.

Every graphic is made to measure: send your wall dimensions and a photo and we'll advise on the right material and layout, then send a proof. Our design studio can create artwork from your brand guidelines or photography.
Wall graphics are one of the most cost-effective ways to transform a space, and most can be removed or updated later as your business changes.

Repositionable wall graphics are the most flexible wall graphic we make. The printed fabric has a low-tack adhesive that lets you peel it off and stick it down again, so you can reposition it during fitting, move it to another wall, or take it with you when you leave a rented office.

The fabric finish is matt and glare-free, with a soft, premium look that suits receptions, showrooms, nurseries, retail displays and events. It's also forgiving to apply: it doesn't stretch like vinyl, so creases and bubbles can simply be lifted and smoothed out.

It's ideal for campaigns that change regularly, temporary exhibitions, pop-up shops and anywhere you want to avoid damaging walls. Store it on its backing sheet between uses and it can be reused several times.

Because fabric has a woven texture, it handles light differently from vinyl. Colours look rich and slightly softer, and there's no reflective shine under spotlights or windows, so the graphic photographs well. That makes it a popular choice for shops, showrooms and event spaces where people take photos.

To fit, peel back a section of the liner, position the top edge, and smooth it down with your hand or a felt squeegee, working from the centre outwards. If it goes on crooked, simply lift and reposition. For large designs supplied in panels, we print a small overlap and alignment marks so the panels match up perfectly.

The adhesive is designed for smooth, painted walls, glass and other smooth surfaces. It's not suitable for textured, wallpapered or freshly painted walls, which should be left to cure for at least four weeks.

Fabric graphics are also a good option where safety and comfort matter. The matt surface doesn't glare under lighting, the material feels soft to the touch, and there are no sharp edges, which is why they're often chosen for nurseries, schools, waiting rooms and children's areas in shops and restaurants.

For businesses with several sites, the same fabric design can be printed in multiple sizes and moved between locations as campaigns change. Keep the original backing sheet, roll the graphic printed side out, and store it flat in a cool, dry place to keep the adhesive clean between uses.

description: A whiteboard wall turns any smooth surface into a dry-wipe writing area for brainstorming, planning and teaching. Gloss dry-wipe vinyl covers whole walls or sections, giving teams far more writing space than a board.

Every graphic is made to measure: send your wall dimensions and a photo and we'll advise on the right material and layout, then send a proof. Our design studio can create artwork from your brand guidelines or photography.
Wall graphics are one of the most cost-effective ways to transform a space, and most can be removed or updated later as your business changes.

A whiteboard wall gives teams far more space to think than a standard board ever could. Cover an entire meeting room wall, a section beside desks, a classroom wall or the side of a cabinet, and everyone can sketch, plan and brainstorm at full size. Because the vinyl is made to measure, it fits around sockets, light switches and door frames neatly, and the finished surface looks sleek and intentional rather than a board screwed to the wall.

The gloss dry-wipe surface works with standard whiteboard markers and wipes clean with a dry cloth or whiteboard eraser. For ghosting from markers left on too long, a whiteboard cleaner restores the surface. You can also print onto the dry-wipe vinyl, adding your logo, a grid, a calendar, a project board layout or a map, so the wall becomes a planning tool that's always ready.

Whiteboard walls are popular in agile offices, project rooms, schools, universities, training centres and creative studios, and in homes too for family planners and kids' rooms. They're also a smart solution in rented offices, where they can be removed later from sound, well-cured paint.

Compared with a framed whiteboard, a whiteboard wall has no frame, no edges in the way and no fixings to work loose. You can write right up to the corners, and multiple people can work on different parts of the wall at the same time. It also costs less per square metre than buying several large boards.

For best results, the wall should be smooth and painted with a satin or silk emulsion that has been left to cure for at least four weeks. Matt paints and fresh plaster can affect adhesion. Any dents or bumps in the wall will show through the gloss surface, so fill and sand any marks before fitting. We're happy to look at photos of your wall and advise.

Planning a whiteboard wall starts with how people will use it. For team stand-ups, a wide, landscape area at standing height works best, with the bottom edge around 800mm from the floor so nobody has to crouch. For classrooms, bring the lower edge down so pupils can reach. For project rooms, run the vinyl edge to edge so every surface becomes usable space.

Printed layouts make the wall work harder. Popular options include a weekly planner with days across the top, a Kanban board with To Do, Doing and Done columns, a sales target tracker, a floor plan, or a faint grid that helps people draw straight lines and tables. Because the print sits beneath the dry-wipe surface, it stays put while the marker wipes away.

Tactile braille signs help everyone use your building independently. Raised letters and pictograms can be read by touch, braille provides the text for braille readers, and high-contrast colours help people with low vision. They're used on toilets, meeting rooms, lifts, stairs and offices.
We make individual signs or complete sets so every door in your building has consistent, accessible signage.

Consistent placement matters for tactile signs: they're normally fixed on the wall on the latch side of the door, at a height where hands can find them easily. We can advise on positioning so your signs are easy to find by touch.
Braille signs can be combined with pictograms, such as toilet, lift or stairs symbols, for faster recognition. Signs are supplied with fixings.
Tactile signs are part of making buildings inclusive. Combined with clear wayfinding, good lighting and colour contrast, they help visitors with sight loss move around confidently.

data.name: Wooden & Slate Signs

description: A wood and metal sign mounts a raised brushed aluminium logo on a warm timber panel. It feels natural and modern at the same time, ideal for cafés, coworking spaces, farm shops and boutique offices.

Natural materials bring warmth and character that plastic and metal can't match, and they suit independent businesses, hospitality and heritage settings especially well. Because wood grain and slate vary naturally, every sign is a little different.
We print or engrave your logo and wording, and send a proof before production. Our studio can adapt your artwork to suit natural materials.
